verdict.rationale: React's own docs describe asynchronous components that fetch data on the server or at build time (react-docs-7), streaming HTML while data loads (react-docs-6), and a 'use client' directive that marks interactive client modules (react-docs-10). Together these outline the server-to-client component architecture. However, the docs say this only works through frameworks that implement it, such as Next.js App Router, so plain React needs an extra framework to deliver the story. Missing for 10: standalone support without a third-party framework, explicit documentation of passing server-fetched data as props across the client boundary (serialization rules), and hands-on or independent corroboration.
